title: Make a Floating Finger With Your Fingertips #science #illusion
description:
Touch your two index fingertips, about a hand's length in front of your eyes, and look past them at something far away. A little floating finger with two tips appears between them. Pull your fingertips apart a bit and it floats in the gap. With your eyes aimed far, your near fingers do not land on matching spots in your two eyes, so each eye sees them in a different place. Your brain lays both views on top of each other, and where the two fingertips overlap you see the floating finger. Look back at your fingers and it is gone.

Most people see it within a few seconds; it can look blurry at first, and it helps to look at a plain, distant background. It needs two eyes that work together, so people with poor binocular vision may not see it.

Sources
- Michael Bach, Optical Illusions and Visual Phenomena: the floating finger illusion (michaelbach.de/ot/sze-Frankfurter)
- Sharp, W. L. (1928). The floating-finger illusion. Psychological Review, 35(2), 171-173
- Myers and DeWall, Psychology in Everyday Life, figure 5.22, the floating finger sausage
- The two-eye views are a drawing, not to scale

Try it: does your floating finger have two nails?
